AffiliationExportReader.description:
Structured affiliation parsed from the author byline. ``text`` is our own
verbatim byline string; the parsed components are best-effort (LLM).
AffiliationExportReader.title: AffiliationExportReader

BibMatchExportReader.description: Flat enrichment match from an external service.
BibMatchExportReader.title: BibMatchExportReader

CitationCandidateExportReader.description: Lossless JSON representation of one citation detector candidate.
CitationCandidateExportReader.title: CitationCandidateExportReader

CitationLinkingExportReader.description: Evidence-bearing diagnostic receipt for inline citation linking.
CitationLinkingExportReader.title: CitationLinkingExportReader

DiagnosticsExportReader.description:
Outcome flags and stage receipts — never raw payloads.

``regions`` and ``trace`` are deliberately NOT here: they are megabyte-scale
intermediate data, and bundling them would force every diagnostics consumer
to reason about size.
DiagnosticsExportReader.title: DiagnosticsExportReader

DoiCandidateExportReader.description:
One source-visible DOI and where it was read.

``page`` and ``region_index`` name the layout region the DOI was read
from: the ``extraction.regions`` row with the same ``page`` and ``index``.
That index is the region's 0-based position among its page's regions after
OCR post-processing. Post-processing renumbers a page when it drops
duplicate regions or merges split ones (a formula and its equation number,
a word hyphenated across two blocks), so the index can differ from the
layout detector's original slot.

A ``sentence`` candidate names the region that began the sentence's
paragraph (``text[].paragraph_id``), which ``region_type`` labels. If the
parser joined following regions into that paragraph, the DOI may be
printed in one of those instead.

``region_index`` is null when no layout region on ``page`` is recorded:
header and footer furniture, structured metadata, captions, footnotes,
input parsed without layout analysis, and a sentence printed on a later
page than the region that began its paragraph.
DoiCandidateExportReader.title: DoiCandidateExportReader

EnrichmentExportReader.description:
Reference-enrichment completeness — lets a consumer distinguish a
partial (timed-out) Crossref enrichment from a complete one without
grepping ``extraction.warnings``. ``null`` when enrichment never ran.
EnrichmentExportReader.title: EnrichmentExportReader

ExtractionExportReader.description:
Extraction provenance — how this output was produced.

Built by ``ExportStage._build_extraction`` from the pipeline context; the
export function passes it through verbatim. Omitted entirely when a Paper is
exported outside the pipeline.
ExtractionExportReader.title: ExtractionExportReader

ExtractionSettingsExportReader.description: Per-run resolutions of the reference/enrichment knobs.
ExtractionSettingsExportReader.title: ExtractionSettingsExportReader

FundingExportReader.description: Structured funding entry parsed from the funding statement.
FundingExportReader.title: FundingExportReader

IdentityExportReader.description: Caller-supplied expectations and the DOI-selection receipt.
IdentityExportReader.title: IdentityExportReader

LlmEngineExportReader.title: LlmEngineExportReader

LlmTraceExportReader.description:
One LLM call's captured prompt and raw response.

Capture is opt-in via ``LLM_CAPTURE_TRACE`` (default off). Traces are joined
to the extraction by paper ID and to usage breakdowns by label, provider,
and model. Credential-shaped tokens are scrubbed before export; document
text is still present, so callers control where trace-bearing exports go.

Only the Instructor backend currently captures traces. The NuExtract-native
backend logs a warning when tracing is requested and emits no trace rows.
Only successful physical attempts are captured: validation re-asks inside
Instructor and transient failures in the outer retry loop are absent.
Consequently ``attempt`` is currently always 1; failure fields do not
constitute a complete retry history.
LlmTraceExportReader.title: LlmTraceExportReader

MetadataExportReader.description:
Scalar paper-level metadata.

Scalars only: nested objects/lists here break R consumers that call
``as.data.frame(metadata)`` (metacheck's ``.read_bibr``). Processing
metadata lives under ``extraction`` instead; file identity under ``source``.
MetadataExportReader.title: MetadataExportReader

MetadataMatchExportReader.description:
Flat enrichment match for the paper's OWN bibliographic identity.

Mirrors :class:`BibMatchExport` (same external-service shape) but keyed to
the paper rather than a reference, so it carries no ``bib_id``.
MetadataMatchExportReader.title: MetadataMatchExportReader

OcrEngineExportReader.description: Which OCR engine produced this output. ``null`` on the DOCX-native path.
OcrEngineExportReader.title: OcrEngineExportReader

PersonNameExportReader.description:
One structured person name.

``literal`` holds corporate/unsplittable names whole (the JATS
``string-name`` analog); when it is set, ``family``/``given`` are absent.
PersonNameExportReader.title: PersonNameExportReader

SourceExportReader.description: Identity of the input artifact — not of the paper.
SourceExportReader.title: SourceExportReader

TimingsExportReader.description:
Per-stage wall-clock seconds (the export stage's own time is excluded —
it is still running when this is built).

Both fields are always populated when this object exists: an untimed run
omits the whole ``extraction.timings`` object rather than emitting one with
null fields (``ExportStage._build_extraction`` passes ``None``, which
``ExtractionExport._omit_absent`` then drops). The ``| None`` types are
structural only.
TimingsExportReader.title: TimingsExportReader

UsageRowExportReader.description: One ``(label, provider, model)`` LLM usage row.
UsageRowExportReader.title: UsageRowExportReader

UsageTotalsExportReader.description: Aggregate of every ``breakdown`` row — denormalized deliberately.
UsageTotalsExportReader.title: UsageTotalsExportReader

ValidationExportReader.description: Promotion disposition derived from typed validation issues.
ValidationExportReader.title: ValidationExportReader

ValidationIssueExportReader.description: JSON-safe representation of a shared pipeline validation issue.
ValidationIssueExportReader.title: ValidationIssueExportReader

description:
Lenient reader for any bibr 11.x JSON export.

Accepts every export the strict v11 schema accepts, plus what the 11.x forward
policy allows: unknown keys at any nesting level, and any ``schema_version`` of
the form ``11.<minor>``. A different major version (``10.x``, ``12.x``), a
missing root ``schema_version``, and a known field with the wrong type are still
rejected.

In Python, unknown keys are kept, not dropped: each model exposes them through
``model_extra`` and includes them in ``model_dump()``. Every nested reader
model subclasses its strict counterpart, so ``isinstance`` checks against
``PaperExport`` and the other strict models still hold.

affiliation.description: Structured author affiliations parsed from the byline: verbatim text plus best-effort institution/department/city/country and linked author IDs.
affiliation.title: Affiliation

author.description: Extracted authors, with name, affiliation, email, corresponding-author flag, ORCID, and contribution roles.
author.title: Author

bib.description: Parsed bibliography entries, verbatim from the printed reference list — never backfilled from external enrichment.
bib.title: Bib

bib_match.description: Flattened enrichment matches (e.g. Crossref) for bibliography entries, one row per external-service hit.
bib_match.title: Bib Match

eq.description: Parsed statistical/mathematical expressions split into left-hand side, degrees of freedom, comparator, and right-hand side.
eq.title: Eq

extraction.description: Extraction provenance: how this output was produced — engines, per-run settings, timings, LLM usage, enrichment, identity receipts, diagnostics and warnings; omitted when exported outside the pipeline.

figure.description: Extracted figures with caption, page number, and (optionally) base64-encoded image data.
figure.title: Figure

funding.description: Structured funder names and award IDs parsed from the funding statement.
funding.title: Funding

metadata.description: Scalar paper-level metadata: title, abstract, keywords, DOI, paper-type and OECD classification, the paper's own journal/venue identity, and research-integrity statement text.

metadata_match.description: Enrichment matches for the paper's own bibliographic identity (self-DOI lookup), shaped like bib_match minus bib_id.
metadata_match.title: Metadata Match

paper_id.description: Paper identifier: user-supplied --paper-id, else the DOI, else the source file name.
paper_id.title: Paper Id

qualification_provenance.description: Deployment-qualification provenance: identity SHAs, per-task protocol hashes, native-validity + fallback outcome, and request counts. Always present; null (never omitted) when no LLM ran or usage tracking is disabled.
qualification_provenance.title: Qualification Provenance

schema_version.description: Export schema version, any 11.x minor. Its presence at the root is how readers distinguish v11 from all earlier versions.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

section.description: Document section headers with hierarchy (level, parent) and IMRaD classification.
section.title: Section

source.description: Identity of the input artifact: file name, content hash, and format.

table.description: Extracted tables with HTML markup, structured cell contents, caption, and page number.
table.title: Table

text.description: Full body text as an ordered array of sentence-level spans, each linked to its paragraph, section, and page.
text.title: Text

url.description: Hyperlinks found in the body text, with their link text and source sentence.
url.title: Url

validation.description: Output validation gate result: counts of errors/warnings and the structured issue list; absent when the gate was skipped.

xref.description: In-text citation/cross-reference markers linking a sentence to a bibliography entry, table, figure, footnote, equation, or section.
xref.title: Xref
